mainTopic: Does שבת make produce obligated in מעשר (קביעות למעשר) even when its processing is not finished?
overview: The amud opens with the end of the משנה's dispute. רבי אליעזר says that on ערב שבת of שביעית a person may point at fruit in the drying area (מוקצה) and say 'from here I will eat tomorrow.' The חכמים say he must mark off an exact area. The גמרא then quotes two משניות about figs. Children who hid figs for שבת must tithe them even after שבת, but figs drying in a חצר may be eaten casually without מעשר. From these, רבא asks רב נחמן whether שבת fixes produce for מעשר even when its processing is not finished. רב נחמן says yes, and when רבא compares שבת to a חצר, he answers that he has an established teaching. מר זוטרא tries to support this from רבי אליעזר's ruling in the משנה, but the גמרא rejects the proof: his own statement fixed the fruit, not שבת. The משנה mentions שבת to teach a different lesson: טבל is מוכן on שבת, because if someone tithed it on שבת anyway, the tithing works.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: Choosing fruit for tomorrow by just saying so
steps.stepSummary: The end of רבי אליעזר's ruling in the משנה: on ערב שבת in שביעית, a person can simply say 'from here I will eat tomorrow' about fruit set aside for drying.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ערב שבת during שביעית, a person may say: 'From here I will eat tomorrow.'
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of the משנה. This line finishes רבי אליעזר's ruling that a simple spoken statement is enough to prepare drying fruit (מוקצה) for eating on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fruit spread out to dry is normally set aside and not meant for eating, so it is מוקצה. רבי אליעזר holds that a general verbal statement the day before is enough to make it ready. The case is set in שביעית so that the only question is מוקצה, with no מעשר issue mixed in.

keyTerms.meaning: Friday, the day before שבת
The seventh, Sabbatical year, when tithes are not taken
'From here I will eat tomorrow', a spoken designation of food

phrases.english: on Shabbat eve during the Sabbatical Year,
and says: From here I will eat tomorrow.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת בַּשְּׁבִיעִית, וְאוֹמֵר: מִכָּאן אֲנִי אוֹכֵל לְמָחָר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, a general verbal designation on ערב שבת is enough to prepare drying fruit for use on שבת.

steps.title: The חכמים: He must mark off an exact area
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree. He must physically mark the fruit and say exactly 'from here until here.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: Not unless he marks it and says, 'From here until there.'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give the opposing view. A vague statement is not enough; he must mark a specific area and name its limits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר accepts a general statement. The חכמים demand a clear, defined boundary, both by marking and by spoken words. The argument is about how specific the preparation has to be.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion
He marks, drawing a physical sign of the boundary
From here until here, a defined area

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends with a dispute. רבי אליעזר says a general statement works; the חכמים require marking plus an exact boundary.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיִּרְשׁוֹם וְיֹאמַר מִכָּאן וְעַד כָּאן.
phrases.english: not unless he marks it and says: From here until there.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: עַד שֶׁיִּרְשׁוֹם וְיֹאמַר מִכָּאן וְעַד כָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי אליעזר's ruling in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, preparing drying fruit for שבת requires marking it and stating a defined boundary.

steps.title: First source: Children who hid figs before שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: children hid figs on ערב שבת and forgot to tithe them. Even after שבת they may not eat them until they tithe.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: Children who hid figs on ערב שבת and forgot and did not tithe them may not eat them on מוצאי שבת unless they tithe them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting an outside משנה. This is setup: it is gathering sources for the question רבא will ask soon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The children hid the figs to eat on שבת, and the figs were not yet a finished product. The ruling shows that שבת made the figs fully obligated in מעשר, so even after שבת a casual snack is no longer allowed. This hints that שבת fixes produce even when it is not finished.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned there, in a משנה elsewhere
They hid or stored away
They separated מעשר (tithes)
Saturday night, after שבת ends

phrases.english: GEMARA:
We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מעשרות 4:2.

phrases.english: Children who hid figs on Shabbat eve
and forgot and did not tithe them,
may not eat them after Shabbat
unless they have tithed them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁטָּמְנוּ תְּאֵנִים מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by bringing an outside source about שבת and מעשר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Figs set aside for שבת become obligated in מעשר, and this obligation stays even after שבת.

steps.title: Second source: Figs drying in a courtyard
steps.stepSummary: A second משנה: figs moved into a courtyard to dry may be eaten casually by the household without מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: We also learned: One who moves figs into his courtyard to dry them, his children and household may eat from them casually and are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second source that seems to point the other way. This is still setup for רבא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חצר normally fixes produce for מעשר. Here, though, the figs are still meant for drying, so their work is not finished, and the חצר does not fix them. Casual eating (עראי) stays permitted. So the חצר fixes only finished produce.

keyTerms.meaning: Courtyard; it can fix produce for מעשר
To dry figs into dried figs
Casual snacking, which does not require מעשר
Exempt

phrases.english: And we also learned:
One who moves figs through his courtyard in order to dry them,
his children and the members of his household
may eat from them casually and are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן נָמֵי: הַמַּעֲבִיר תְּאֵנִים בַּחֲצֵרוֹ לְקַצּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source to set beside the first: the חצר does not fix unfinished produce.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חצר does not fix produce for מעשר when its work is not yet finished.

steps.title: רבא asks: Does שבת fix unfinished produce for מעשר?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן whether שבת obligates מוקצה produce in מעשר even when its work is not finished. Maybe yes, because of 'call שבת a delight.' Or maybe שבת works only on finished produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: Does שבת fix מוקצה produce for tithes when its work is not finished? Do we say that since it is written 'And call שבת a delight,' it fixes even unfinished produce? Or perhaps it fixes finished produce but not unfinished produce?
steps.whatsHappening: Building on the two sources, רבא asks a clear question with two sides: does שבת fix produce for מעשר even before its processing is complete?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: because the פסוק calls שבת a 'delight,' any eating on שבת counts as a real meal, so it fixes even unfinished produce. Side two: maybe שבת is like other things that fix produce and works only once the produce is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him
It fixes, making produce obligated in מעשר
Produce set aside, here fruit put away for drying
Its processing is finished
Delight

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'קביעה' means making food obligated in מעשר. It does not mean fixing a meal time, and it does not mean the שבת prohibition of מוקצה.

phrases.english: Rava asked Rav Nachman:
Shabbat, what is the law: does it fix set-aside produce for tithing
in an item whose work is not finished?
Do we say, since it is written:
"And call Shabbat a delight,"

phrases.aramaic: קָבְעָה וַאֲפִילּוּ בְּדָבָר שֶׁלֹּא נִגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתּוֹ,
phrases.english: it fixes even an item whose work is not finished,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: בְּדָבָר שֶׁנִּגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתּוֹ — קָבְעָה,
phrases.english: or perhaps: an item whose work is finished, it fixes,

phrases.aramaic: בְּדָבָר שֶׁלֹּא נִגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתּוֹ — לָא קָבְעָה?
phrases.english: but an item whose work is not finished, it does not fix?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the two sources to raise a question: is שבת more powerful than a חצר?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether שבת fixes produce for מעשר even when the produce's processing is not complete.
steps.whyThisMatters: This defines how strong שבת is in creating a מעשר obligation compared with other things that fix produce, such as a חצר.

steps.title: רב נחמן: שבת fixes both kinds
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that שבת fixes produce for מעשר whether its work is finished or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: שבת fixes both an item whose work is finished and an item whose work is not finished.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a direct answer and chooses the first side of רבא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבת is stronger than a חצר. It fixes produce for מעשר even before the produce is finished. This fits the children's figs, which needed מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixes, making the produce obligated

keyTerms.term: בֵּין בְּדָבָר שֶׁנִּגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתּוֹ בֵּין בְּדָבָר שֶׁלֹּא נִגְמְרָה מְלַאכְתּוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: Whether its work is finished or not

phrases.english: He said to him: Shabbat fixes,
both an item whose work is finished,
and an item whose work is not finished.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שבת fixes produce for מעשר whether or not its processing is complete.

steps.title: רבא challenges: Shouldn't שבת be like a חצר?
steps.stepSummary: רבא pushes back. Compare שבת to a חצר: a חצר fixes only finished produce, so שבת should also fix only finished produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But say שבת is like a חצר. Just as a חצר fixes only an item whose work is finished, so too שבת should fix only an item whose work is finished!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב נחמן's answer with a comparison to the חצר from the second source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both a חצר and שבת are things that fix produce for מעשר. A חצר is limited to finished produce, so logic suggests שבת should share the same limit. That would contradict רב נחמן's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: But say, introducing a counter-suggestion
Similar to
Just as... so too..., a comparison formula

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְאֵימָא שַׁבָּת דּוּמְיָא דְחָצֵר,
phrases.english: He said to him: But say Shabbat is like a courtyard:
phrases.notes: Now רבא is the one speaking, pushing back on רב נחמן.

phrases.english: just as a courtyard does not fix
except an item whose work is finished,
so too Shabbat should not fix
except an item whose work is finished!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְאֵימָא שַׁבָּת דּוּמְיָא דְחָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's answer in step 6 using the חצר source from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that שבת fixes even unfinished produce.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A comparison: since a חצר, which also fixes produce, works only on finished produce, שבת should be limited the same way.

steps.title: רב נחמן: This is an established teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that this is not just his own reasoning. He has a clear, established teaching that שבת fixes both finished and unfinished produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We have an established teaching in our hands that שבת fixes both an item whose work is finished and an item whose work is not finished.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his ruling. It rests on a received tradition, not on logic that a comparison could overturn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's attack used logic, comparing שבת to a חצר. רב נחמן answers that a firm, established tradition outweighs such a comparison. His ruling therefore stands.

keyTerms.meaning: An established, well-ordered teaching
In our hands, meaning we have it as a tradition

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן rules that שבת fixes produce for מעשר even when its processing is not finished. This makes שבת stronger than a חצר, and the ruling rests on an established tradition.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a clear received teaching can override a logical comparison. It sets שבת apart from a חצר in the laws of מעשר.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תַּלְמוּד עָרוּךְ הוּא בְּיָדֵינוּ
phrases.english: He said to him: We have an established teaching in our hands
that Shabbat fixes,
both an item whose work is finished,
and an item whose work is not finished.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תַּלְמוּד עָרוּךְ הוּא בְּיָדֵינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from step 7 and confirms the ruling from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to an established tradition over a logical comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שבת should be like a חצר and fix only finished produce.
steps.terutzMaskana: An established teaching says שבת fixes both finished and unfinished produce, so the comparison to a חצר is set aside.

steps.title: מר זוטרא brings support from רבי אליעזר's teaching in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא supports רב נחמן from the משנה. It allows choosing drying-yard fruit before שבת only in שביעית, which suggests that in other years שבת would fix even this unfinished produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא, son of רב נחמן, said: our משנה supports this too. רבי אליעזר says a person may stand over the drying-yard fruit on ערב שבת in שביעית (and say 'from here I'll eat tomorrow'). The reason is that שביעית fruit is never tithed. So in other years it would be forbidden. Why? Isn't it because שבת fixes the produce, even though it is still unfinished?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן's son brings a proof from a משנה to back up his father's ruling: שבת fixes produce for מעשר even when its work is not finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fruit in the מוקצה is still drying, so its work is not finished. The משנה permits choosing it only in שביעית, which implies that in a normal year it would need tithing. The proof assumes the thing doing the fixing is שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it: a formula for bringing support from a משנה or ברייתא
Here: the drying area where figs or grapes are spread out. Their work is not yet finished.
The seventh (Sabbatical) year, whose produce is exempt from מעשר
שבת fixes the produce, making it obligated in מעשר

steps.confusionAlert: Here מוקצה does NOT mean the familiar 'set-aside object you can't move on שבת.' It means the drying yard for fruit whose processing is unfinished.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra, son of Rav Nachman, said:
We too have learned this in a Mishnah:
And Rabbi Eliezer further said:
A person may stand over the drying-yard produce
phrases.notes: This is fruit still drying out, so its work isn't finished yet.

phrases.english: on Shabbat eve in the Sabbatical Year, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' stands for the rest of the משנה, where he says: 'From here I will eat tomorrow.'

phrases.english: The reason is that it is the Sabbatical Year,
whose produce is not subject to tithing.
But in the other years of the seven-year cycle,
it would indeed be forbidden to eat it untithed.
What is the reason?
Is it not because Shabbat fixes it for tithing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds outside support from a משנה to רב נחמן's teaching (Step 8).
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's ruling that שבת fixes even unfinished produce for מעשר
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר's משנה about choosing drying-yard fruit on ערב שבת in שביעית

steps.title: The proof is rejected: his words fixed the meal, not שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. What fixed the produce was his statement 'from here I will eat tomorrow,' not שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, that case is different. Since he said 'From here I will eat tomorrow,' he has set this produce aside for a meal, and that is what fixes it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on מר זוטרא's proof by giving a different reason why the produce would need tithing in a normal year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying out loud that he will eat this fruit as a meal tomorrow fixes it all by itself. So the משנה's case does not show that שבת fixes unfinished produce, and the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: There it is different: a standard way to reject a proof by showing the case is special
'From here I will eat tomorrow': his designating statement
He fixed (a meal) on it for himself

phrases.english: No, there it is different:
since he said, 'From here I will eat tomorrow,'
he has fixed it for himself for a meal.
phrases.notes: His own words, not שבת, are what make the fruit need tithing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. רב נחמן's ruling itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed שבת was what fixed the produce. In fact his own statement fixed it.

steps.title: If his words fix it, why does the משנה mention שבת at all?
steps.stepSummary: If his statement is what fixes the produce, the same should be true on a weekday. So why does the משנה say ערב שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why mention שבת in particular? Even on a weekday it should be the same!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection it just gave: if שבת plays no role, the משנה's mention of שבת seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rejection in Step 10 makes שבת irrelevant to the fixing. But the משנה specifically sets the case on ערב שבת, so the גמרא wants to know why that detail is there.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a challenge that follows from what was just said
Why specifically this case? (it should apply more widely)
A weekday

phrases.english: If so, why mention Shabbat in particular?
Even on a weekday it would also be so!

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that his statement, not שבת, fixed the produce
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a spoken designation fixes the produce, then שבת adds nothing, and the משנה's mention of ערב שבת would be pointless.

steps.title: The משנה mentions שבת to teach that טבל is not מוקצה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה mentions שבת to teach that טבל counts as prepared (מוכן) for שבת. If someone tithed it on שבת anyway, it is properly fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is teaching us that טבל is considered ready for use on שבת. If someone broke the rule and tithed it on שבת, it is tithed, and he may eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing that the משנה mentions שבת for a different lesson, about whether טבל is מוקצה on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think טבל is מוקצה on שבת, since you are not allowed to tithe on שבת and so cannot eat it. The משנה teaches that it is still מוכן, because tithing it on שבת, though forbidden, does work. This ends the attempted proof: the משנה gives no support to the idea that שבת fixes unfinished produce.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches us: points to the new lesson the source is coming to teach
Produce from which תרומות and מעשרות have not yet been separated
Prepared, ready for use on שבת (the opposite of מוקצה)
He transgressed and fixed it (separated the tithes)

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from רבי אליעזר's משנה fails: his statement 'from here I will eat tomorrow' is what fixed the produce. The mention of שבת teaches something else: טבל is מוכן on שבת, because tithing it on שבת after the fact does work.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that טבל is not מוקצה on שבת. If someone wrongly tithed it on שבת, the produce may be eaten.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
that untithed produce is considered ready for Shabbat,
for if he transgressed and fixed it by tithing,
it is fixed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11 and keeps the rejection of Step 10 standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets why the source mentions שבת: it is there for a different lesson, about מוקצה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: You would think the mention of שבת means שבת is what fixes the produce, or else the detail is useless.
steps.terutzMaskana: שבת is mentioned to teach that טבל is מוכן on שבת, since tithing it on שבת after the fact works.
